mainTopic: Drashos on the names of כלב and מרים, and the story of עמרם, יוכבד and the birth and hiding of משה.
overview: The גמרא first proves from the word 'הקנזי' that כלב was raised by קנז, his stepfather. It then reads the names in פסוקים in דברי הימים as hints to כלב and his wife מרים. עזובה, יריעות, חלאה and נערה tell how מרים went from sick and abandoned to healthy and beautiful. ישר, שובב, אשחור and תקוע praise כלב, and רבי יוחנן learns that whoever marries a woman לשם שמים is considered as if he gave birth to her. The גמרא then returns to מצרים: פרעה made three decrees, each harsher than the one before. עמרם divorced his wife because of the decree, but מרים convinced him to take her back, and he made a full new wedding. The פסוקים about משה's birth teach that יוכבד became young again at 130, gave birth without pain, and hid משה for three months. The amud ends with drashos about the reed basket and its coatings, and a disagreement about the word 'בסוף' that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The word 'הקנזי' supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings support for רבא's claim that כלב was the stepson of קנז: the פסוק calls כלב 'הקנזי' even though his father was יפונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also shown by the exact wording, since it is written 'הקנזי.' Conclude from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is backing up רבא's earlier claim that כלב was the stepson of קנז. It points to a פסוק that calls כלב 'the Kenizzite.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: כלב is called בן יפונה, so why is he also called 'הקנזי'? This makes sense if קנז was his stepfather who raised him, which is exactly what רבא said. The גמרא accepts the support with 'שמע מינה.'

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise; the exact words of a text support the idea
The Kenizzite, a name connected to קנז
Conclude from it; the proof is accepted

phrases.english: It is also precise
as it is written: "the Kenizzite."
phrases.notes: יהושע 14:6. כלב's father was יפונה, yet the פסוק still calls him the Kenizzite.

phrases.english: Conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's statement from the previous section that כלב was קנז's stepson.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that כלב was the stepson of קנז
steps.raayaSupportSource: The title 'הקנזי' given to כלב in יהושע 14:6, even though his father was יפונה

steps.title: עזובה is מרים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining the פסוק about כלב's wife. עזובה is really מרים, and she is called this because everyone first abandoned her.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'עזובה' is מרים. Why is she called עזובה? Because at first everyone abandoned her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts going word by word through a פסוק about כלב's family. It says the wife named עזובה is actually מרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name עזובה comes from the root עזב, 'to leave.' The דרשה reads the name as describing her life: at first no one wanted to marry her. This sets up the next lines, which praise כלב for marrying her.

keyTerms.meaning: עזובה, a name meaning 'the abandoned one'

phrases.english: "Azubah" — this is Miriam,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 2:18: 'And כלב son of חצרון fathered children with עזובה his wife, and with יריעות.'

phrases.english: and why is she called Azubah?
Because everyone abandoned her at first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new section explaining the פסוק in דברי הימים about כלב's wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עזובה in the פסוק is מרים, named this way because at first everyone left her and did not want to marry her.

steps.title: Why does the verse say 'fathered'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק says כלב 'הוליד' (fathered) with עזובה, when really he married her.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Fathered' — but wasn't he marrying her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices strange wording in the פסוק and asks about it. The question sets up רבי יוחנן's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If עזובה is כלב's wife, the natural word would be 'married,' not 'הוליד,' which means fathered or gave birth. The גמרא wants to know what this odd word is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: He fathered; he gave birth to

phrases.english: "Fathered" —
but wasn't he marrying her?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹלִיד וַהֲלֹא מִינְסָב הֲוָה נָסֵיב לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues through the same פסוק and questions its word 'הוליד.'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the פסוק use 'הוליד' for a man marrying his wife?

steps.title: Marrying for the sake of Heaven is like giving birth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that whoever marries a woman לשם שמים gets credit from the פסוק as if he gave birth to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Whoever marries a woman לשם שמים, the פסוק counts it for him as if he gave birth to her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question about the word 'הוליד.' He explains that the word is praising כלב for why he married מרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כלב married מרים לשם שמים, even though everyone else had left her. Because of this, the פסוק treats it as if he gave her a new life, so it says 'הוליד.' The odd word becomes a lesson that applies to anyone who marries for the right reasons.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of Heaven; for pure reasons
The פסוק credits him; it counts it for him
As if he gave birth to her

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: whoever marries a woman לשם שמים is considered as if he gave birth to her. This is learned from the word 'הוליד' about כלב and מרים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known teaching about the great value of a marriage built on pure motives.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Anyone who marries a woman for the sake of Heaven —
the verse credits him
as if he gave birth to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כׇּל הַנּוֹשֵׂא אִשָּׁה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about why the פסוק says 'הוליד.'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'הוליד' teaches that marrying a woman לשם שמים is counted as if he gave birth to her.

steps.title: יריעות describes מרים's face
steps.stepSummary: The second name in the פסוק, יריעות, is also מרים. It describes her face, which looked like curtains.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'יריעות' — because her face looked like curtains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next name in the פסוק, יריעות. It says this is another name for מרים, describing how her face looked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to list a second wife, יריעות. The גמרא reads it as another description of מרים. The name sounds like יריעות, 'curtains,' and it describes her pale, unhealthy look.

keyTerms.meaning: Curtains; also the name יריעות in the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: יריעות is not a second wife of כלב. The גמרא reads it as another name for the same woman, מרים.

phrases.english: "Jerioth" —
because her face looked like curtains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to the next word in the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יריעות is another name for מרים, describing her face, which looked like curtains.

steps.title: Read it as 'her builders,' not 'her sons'
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'ואלה בניה' is read as 'בוניה,' her builders. So the names that follow describe her husband כלב, not her children.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And these are her sons' — do not read it as 'her sons' but as 'her builders.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes how one word is read, using the method 'אל תקרי.' This sets up the next step, which explains the names that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply read, the names after 'ואלה בניה' would be מרים's children. By reading 'בוניה,' her builders, the גמרא turns them into names for כלב, who 'built' her by marrying her.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read it as…; a method that reads a word in a different way to learn a lesson

steps.confusionAlert: 'אל תקרי' does not mean the written word is wrong. It adds a second reading next to the plain one to teach a lesson.

phrases.english: "And these are her sons" —
do not read "her sons"
but rather "her builders,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues through the פסוק to the phrase 'ואלה בניה.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The names after 'ואלה בניה' describe the one who 'built' מרים, her husband כלב, not her children.

steps.title: ישר, שובב, and ארדון describe כלב
steps.stepSummary: The three names describe כלב: ישר, he made himself straight; שובב, he broke his יצר; ארדון, he ruled over his יצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'ישר' — he set himself straight. 'שובב' — he broke his יצר. 'וארדון' — he ruled over his יצר.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the names are about כלב, the גמרא explains each one as describing his good character.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each name is tied to a word that sounds like it. ישר is linked to 'יישר,' straightened. שובב is linked to 'שיבב,' broke. ארדון is linked to 'רדה,' ruled. Together they show כלב as someone who controlled his יצר.

phrases.english: "Jesher" — because he set himself straight.
"Shobab" — because he broke his inclination,
"And Ardon" — because he ruled over his inclination,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reading 'בוניה' to explain each name as a description of כלב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישר, שובב, and ארדון are names for כלב that describe his straightness and his control over his יצר.

steps.title: Another view: ארדון refers to מרים's rose-like face
steps.stepSummary: A second opinion says the name ארדון refers to מרים, whose face became like a rose (ורד).
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: because her face looked like a rose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second explanation of the name ארדון. This view says it describes מרים's face, not כלב's control of his יצר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view linked ארדון to 'רדה,' ruled. This view links it to 'ורד,' a rose. That fits the story: after her marriage, מרים's pale, curtain-like face became beautiful like a rose.
steps.whatToRemember: In this פסוק every name is read as a lesson. עזובה, יריעות, and ארדון (in the second view) describe מרים. ישר, שובב, and ארדון (in the first view) describe כלב, who married her לשם שמים.

phrases.english: And some say:
because her face looked like a rose.
phrases.notes: This view hears 'ורד' (rose) in the name וארדון, so here the name describes מרים, not כלב.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי עַל שֶׁהָיוּ פָּנֶיהָ דּוֹמִין לְוֶרֶד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation of the name ארדון from the one in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ארדון describes מרים, whose face became like a rose.

steps.title: אשחור, father of תקוע, is כלב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new פסוק and reads the names אשחור, אבי, and תקוע as descriptions of כלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And אשחור the father of תקוע had two wives, חלאה and נערה.' אשחור is כלב. Why is he called אשחור? Because his face turned black from fasting. 'Father of' means he became like a father to her (מרים). 'תקוע' means he fixed his heart on his Father in Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another פסוק from דברי הימים and explains that each name in it is really a description of כלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works the same way as the earlier steps: a name in the פסוק is read as a hint to a quality. אשחור sounds like שחור (black), so it points to his fasting. תקוע sounds like תקע (fixed firmly), so it points to his strong connection to ה'.

keyTerms.meaning: A name in the פסוק, read here as כָּלֵב
His Father in Heaven, meaning ה'

phrases.english: "And Ashhur the father of Tekoa
had two wives, Helah and Naarah."
"Ashhur": this is Caleb.
And why was he called "Ashhur"?
Because his face was blackened by fasts.
phrases.notes: This is a wordplay: אשחור sounds like שחור, black.

phrases.english: "The father of": because he became like a father to her.
phrases.notes: "Her" is מרים, his wife, whom he took care of.

phrases.english: "Tekoa": because he fixed his heart
on his Father in Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְאַשְׁחוּר אֲבִי תְקוֹעַ הָיוּ שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading names in דברי הימים as hints to כלב and מרים, now using a new פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אשחור, אבי, and תקוע all describe כלב: he fasted, he was like a father to מרים, and he attached himself to ה'.

steps.title: מרים was like two different women
steps.stepSummary: 'Two wives' does not mean two women. It means מרים changed so much that she was like two people: first sick, later young and healthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Had two wives' means מרים became like two women. חלאה and נערה were not two separate women. At first she was sickly (חלאה), and in the end she was like a young woman (נערה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the 'two wives' in the same פסוק. They are really one woman, מרים, at two different stages of her life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain פסוק sounds like כלב had two wives. The דרשה turns this into one wife who changed. חלאה sounds like חולי, sickness, and נערה means a young girl. So the two names describe her 'before' and 'after.'

keyTerms.meaning: A name in the פסוק, read as 'sickly'

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as כלב having two wives. The גמרא is saying both names belong to the same woman, מרים.

phrases.english: "Had two wives":
Miriam became like two women.
"Helah and Naarah":
there were not really a Helah and a Naarah.
Rather, at first she was sickly,
and in the end she was a young woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים — נַעֲשָׂה מִרְיָם כִּשְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of the same פסוק begun in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חלאה and נערה are one woman, מרים: sick at first, young and healthy at the end.

steps.title: צרת, צהר, and אתנן describe מרים's beauty
steps.stepSummary: The 'children of Helah' are read as three more names for מרים, each describing her new beauty.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the children of חלאה were צרת, צהר, and אתנן.' צרת: she became a rival to the other women. צהר: her face shone like noon. אתנן: any man who saw her brought a gift to his own wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next פסוק and reads the three 'children' as three more names for מרים after she was healed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as 'her children' earlier were read as describing כלב, here the 'children' describe מרים herself. Each name is a wordplay: צרת and צרה (rival), צהר and צהרים (noon), אתנן (a gift).

keyTerms.meaning: A rival, someone others are jealous of
Noon, when the sun is brightest

steps.whatToRemember: The whole set of names in דברי הימים tells one story: כלב married מרים לשם שמים, cared for her, and she went from sick to beautiful.

phrases.english: "And the children of Helah were Zereth, Zohar, and Ethnan."
"Zereth": because she became a rival to the other women.
"Zohar": because her face shone like noon.
"Ethnan": because anyone who saw her
would bring a gift to his own wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from 'Helah' in step 10 into the next פסוק, finishing the drashos about מרים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צרת, צהר, and אתנן are all descriptions of מרים's beauty after she was healed.

steps.title: פרעה decreed even against his own people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the story in מצרים. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says פרעה's decree to throw baby boys in the river also covered Egyptian babies.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And פרעה commanded all his people.' רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: he made a decree even against his own people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the names in דברי הימים and goes back to the פסוקים about פרעה. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא learns that the decree included Egyptian babies too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says פרעה commanded 'all his people' to throw every boy into the river. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא reads this as including Egyptian boys too, not just Jewish ones. This sets up his next teaching about three decrees.

phrases.english: "And Pharaoh commanded all his people."
Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Hanina, said:
He made the decree even against his own people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about כלב and מרים and goes back to the main story of the slavery in מצרים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פרעה's decree to throw the boys into the river applied even to Egyptian babies.

steps.title: פרעה's three decrees
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא lists three decrees from פרעה, each one harsher than the one before.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא also said: פרעה made three decrees. First: 'If it is a son, kill him.' Next: 'Every son that is born, throw into the river.' Finally, he decreed even against his own people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא puts פרעה's decrees in order, showing how they got worse step by step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first decree was a quiet order to the midwives. The second was a public order to throw Jewish boys into the river. The third went so far that it included Egyptian babies too, which is the teaching from step 12.
steps.whatToRemember: פרעה made three decrees: (1) the midwives should kill the boys, (2) throw Jewish boys into the river, (3) even Egyptian boys.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Hanina, said:
He made three decrees.
First: "If it is a son, you shall kill him."
phrases.notes: שמות 1:16. This was his order to the midwives.

phrases.english: Then: "Every son that is born, you shall throw into the river."
And finally, he made the decree even against his own people.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: שָׁלֹשׁ גְּזֵירוֹת גָּזַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same speaker builds on step 12 and places that decree as the third and harshest of three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פרעה made three decrees in order: kill the boys at birth, throw Jewish boys into the river, and finally include Egyptian boys too.

steps.title: Where did the man from לוי go?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק "וילך איש מבית לוי" and asks what 'went' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And there went a man of the house of לוי.' To where did he go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new פסוק about עמרם and asks a question about one word in it. This sets up the answer and the story that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the man 'went,' but it never says where. The גמרא treats this extra word as a hint that something happened before the marriage. The next step answers what it was.

phrases.english: "And there went a man of the house of Levi."
To where did he go?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After listing פרעה's decrees, the גמרא turns to the next פסוק in the story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'went' mean, since no place is mentioned?

steps.title: He went by his daughter's advice
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בר זבינא explains that 'went' means he followed his daughter's advice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בר זבינא said: He 'went' by following his daughter's advice.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה בר זבינא answers the question. 'Went' does not mean he traveled somewhere. It means he acted on what his daughter told him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'went' is read as going along with someone's advice, not physical walking. The story that comes next explains what that advice was.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda bar Zevina said:
He went according to the advice of his daughter.
phrases.notes: The daughter is מרים, as the next steps will show.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Went' means he acted on his daughter's advice.

steps.title: עמרם divorces his wife, and everyone follows
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says עמרם was the leader of his generation. Because of פרעה's decree, he divorced his wife, and all the others did the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: עמרם was the greatest man of his generation. When he saw that wicked פרעה said, 'Every son that is born, throw into the river,' he said, 'We are working for nothing.' So he divorced his wife, and everyone else divorced their wives too.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives the background to the advice. עמרם thought having children was pointless if they would be killed, so he divorced his wife. Everyone copied him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because עמרם was the leader, his actions became everyone's actions. That is why his choice mattered so much. It sets up מרים's argument in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The great man of the generation

phrases.english: It was taught: Amram was the great man of the generation.
Once he saw that the wicked Pharaoh said
"Every son that is born, you shall throw into the river,"
he said: We are laboring for nothing,
He arose and divorced his wife.
All of them arose and divorced their wives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the story behind 'his daughter's advice.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עמרם divorced his wife because of פרעה's decree, and all of Israel followed him.

steps.title: מרים: your decree is harsher than פרעה's
steps.stepSummary: מרים tells עמרם his decree is worse than פרעה's. It affects girls too, and it takes away the World-to-Come.
steps.simpleTranslation: His daughter said to him: Father, your decree is harsher than פרעה's. פרעה decreed only against the boys, but you decreed against the boys and the girls. פרעה decreed only in this world, but you decreed in this world and in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: מרים challenges her father's decision. She gives the first two reasons why it is worse than פרעה's decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no babies are born, then no girls are born either, even though פרעה let girls live. A baby who is killed still gets עולם הבא, but a baby who is never born gets nothing at all.

phrases.english: His daughter said to him: Father,
your decree is harsher than that of Pharaoh.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁפַּרְעֹה לֹא גָּזַר אֶלָּא עַל הַזְּכָרִים,
phrases.english: For Pharaoh decreed only on the males,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַתָּה גָּזַרְתָּ עַל הַזְּכָרִים וְעַל הַנְּקֵיבוֹת.
phrases.english: but you decreed on the males and on the females.

phrases.aramaic: פַּרְעֹה לָא גָּזַר אֶלָּא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
phrases.english: Pharaoh decreed only in this world,
but you, in this world and in the World-to-Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרָה לוֹ בִּתּוֹ: אַבָּא, קָשָׁה גְּזֵירָתְךָ יוֹתֵר מִשֶּׁל פַּרְעֹה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: מרים challenges the decision described in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: עמרם's decision to divorce his wife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not having children hurts both boys and girls. It also takes away their World-to-Come, so it is worse than פרעה's decree.

steps.title: A צדיק's decree always comes true
steps.stepSummary: מרים's third point: פרעה's decree might fail, but a צדיק's decree is sure to happen, as a פסוק in איוב shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: With wicked פרעה, maybe his decree will happen and maybe it won't. But you are a צדיק, so your decree will certainly happen, as it says: 'You shall decree a thing, and it shall be established for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: מרים gives her third and strongest reason, and she backs it up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פרעה's decree might be stopped. But ה׳ fulfills what a צדיק decides, so עמרם's decree would surely come true. That makes it more dangerous than פרעה's.

phrases.english: Pharaoh the wicked:
maybe his decree will be fulfilled,
maybe it will not be fulfilled.
You are a righteous man;
certainly your decree will be fulfilled,
as it is stated: "You shall decree a thing, and it shall be established for you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues מרים's challenge with a third point and a פסוק to support it.
steps.kashyaTarget: עמרם's decision to divorce his wife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A צדיק's decree is sure to come true, while פרעה's might fail.

steps.title: עמרם takes his wife back, and everyone follows
steps.stepSummary: עמרם accepts מרים's argument and remarries his wife. All of Israel does the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: He arose and took back his wife, and all of them arose and took back their wives.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. עמרם listens to his daughter and remarries his wife, and everyone follows him again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ending explains the פסוק: 'a man went' by his daughter's advice 'and took a daughter of לוי.' That means he married her again. Just as everyone followed him in divorcing, everyone followed him in remarrying.
steps.whatToRemember: 'וילך איש מבית לוי' means עמרם followed מרים's advice. She showed him that refusing to have children was worse than פרעה's decree in three ways: it hurts girls too, it takes away עולם הבא, and a צדיק's decree is sure to come true. So he remarried his wife, and all of Israel did the same.

phrases.english: He arose and brought back his wife,
all of them arose and brought back their wives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: עמרם accepts מרים's challenge.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: עמרם followed his daughter's advice and remarried his wife. This is the 'going' in the פסוק, and all of Israel followed his example.

steps.title: Why does the verse say 'took' instead of 'returned'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק says עמרם 'took' יוכבד, since he was only taking back the wife he had divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'and he took.' It should have said 'and he returned'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking the wording of the פסוק. עמרם was remarrying his old wife, so 'took' sounds like a first marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said עמרם took back the wife he had divorced. But the פסוק uses the word for a brand-new marriage. The גמרא wants to know why the פסוק chose that word.

keyTerms.meaning: And he took (the usual word for marrying a wife)

phrases.english: "And he took."
It should have said "and he returned"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the conclusion of Step 19 (עמרם remarried) and checks it against the wording of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A remarriage should be described as 'returning' a wife, not 'taking' one.

steps.title: He made her a full new wedding
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בר זבינא answers that עמרם made a whole wedding, as if it were the first time, with אהרן and מרים dancing and angels singing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בר זבינא said: He made a full wedding for her. He sat her on a wedding carriage, אהרן and מרים danced in front of her, and the angels said: 'A joyful mother of children.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The פסוק says 'took' because עמרם celebrated the remarriage like a brand-new wedding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Took' is not a mistake. It tells us how the remarriage was done: with a full wedding celebration. The angels' words come from a פסוק in תהלים about a happy mother.

keyTerms.meaning: The acts of a (first) marriage, a full wedding
A wedding carriage or canopied seat

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda bar Zevina said:
That he performed an act of marriage —
He sat her on a wedding carriage,
and Aaron and Miriam danced before her,
and the ministering angels said:
"A joyful mother of children."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר זְבִינָא: שֶׁעָשָׂה לוֹ מַעֲשֵׂה לִיקּוּחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20's question about the word 'took'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the wording: 'took' describes a full wedding ceremony.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Took' seemed like the wrong word for a remarriage.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Took' is exact, because עמרם celebrated a complete new wedding.

steps.title: How can a 130-year-old woman be called 'a daughter'?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק calls יוכבד 'a daughter of לוי,' but she was 130 years old at the time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'a daughter of לוי.' Is that possible? She was 130 years old, and it calls her 'a daughter'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the next words of the פסוק. 'Daughter' sounds like a young girl, but יוכבד was very old.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בת' usually describes a young woman. The גמרא says יוכבד was 130, so the word seems out of place. The next step brings the source that shows she was really that old.

phrases.english: "A daughter of Levi."

phrases.aramaic: אֶפְשָׁר בַּת מֵאָה וּשְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה הָוְיָא
phrases.english: Is it possible? She was 130 years old,
and it calls her "a daughter"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶפְשָׁר בַּת מֵאָה וּשְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה הָוְיָא וְקָרֵי לַהּ ״בַּת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next phrase of the same פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A 130-year-old woman would not normally be called 'a daughter'.

steps.title: Proof that יוכבד was born as the family entered Egypt
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא teaches that יוכבד was conceived on the way to Egypt and born inside Egypt. This is the source for her age of 130.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: This is יוכבד. She was conceived on the road and born between the walls, as it says: 'whom she bore to לוי in Egypt.' Her birth was in Egypt, but her conception was not in Egypt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the claim that יוכבד was 130. It shows she was born just as יעקב's family arrived in Egypt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words 'in Egypt' in the פסוק teach that only her birth was in Egypt, not her conception. So she was born right at the start of the time in Egypt. Counting the years in Egypt until משה was born gives her age as 130.

keyTerms.meaning: Her conception (when her mother became pregnant with her)
Between the walls, meaning inside Egypt

phrases.english: As Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said:
This is Yocheved,
whose conception was on the road,
phrases.notes: The road is the trip יעקב's family made down to Egypt.

phrases.english: and her birth was between the walls,
as it is stated:
"Who was born to Levi in Egypt" —
her birth was in Egypt,
but her conception was not in Egypt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the starting point of Step 22's question (that יוכבד was 130).
steps.raayaObject: That יוכבד was 130 years old when משה was born
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 26:59, read as 'born in Egypt but not conceived in Egypt'

steps.title: She became young again
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers that the signs of youth returned to יוכבד, so she could rightly be called 'a daughter.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: The signs of a young woman came back to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 22. The פסוק calls her 'a daughter' because she miraculously became young again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that 'בת' does not fit an old woman. The answer keeps both facts: she was 130, and her body became young again. So the word 'בת' really does describe her.

keyTerms.meaning: Signs of youth, the features of a young woman

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
That the signs of a young woman were born in her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: שֶׁנּוֹלְדוּ בָּהּ סִימָנֵי נַעֲרוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22 after Step 23 showed she was really 130.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the word through a miracle: she became young again.
steps.terutzMaskana: She regained the signs of youth, so 'בת' fits.

steps.title: She was already pregnant, so why say 'she conceived'?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says יוכבד conceived and bore a son, but she was already three months pregnant with משה before עמרם took her back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And the woman conceived and bore a son.' But she was already pregnant with him for three months from before!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the next פסוק. Why mention her conceiving if she was already pregnant?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order in the פסוק makes it sound like she got pregnant only after the remarriage. But the גמרא holds that she was already three months pregnant. So the word 'conceived' seems unneeded or out of place.

phrases.english: "And the woman conceived and bore a son."
But she was already pregnant with him
for three months from the start!
phrases.notes: This means before עמרם took her back. The גמרא explains this later.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הֲוָת מִיעַבְּרָא בֵּיהּ תְּלָתָא יַרְחֵי מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק (שמות 2:2) about משה's birth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: She was already pregnant before the remarriage, so the פסוק should not need to say she conceived.

steps.title: The birth is compared to the conception: both without pain
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בר זבינא answers that the פסוק puts 'conceived' next to 'bore' to compare them. Just as her pregnancy began without pain, she gave birth without pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בר זבינא said: The פסוק compares her giving birth to her becoming pregnant. Just as becoming pregnant was without pain, so too giving birth was without pain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The word 'conceived' is there to teach something about the birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts the two words side by side so we will learn one from the other. Becoming pregnant has no pain. So the פסוק is telling us יוכבד's birth had no pain either.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares, puts two things side by side to learn one from the other

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda bar Zevina said:
It compares her giving birth to her becoming pregnant:
just as her becoming pregnant was without pain,
so too her giving birth was without pain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר זְבִינָא: מַקִּישׁ לֵידָתָהּ לְהוֹרָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 25's question about the word 'conceived'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word a new purpose: it is a comparison, not a time marker.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Conceived' seemed to say she became pregnant only after the remarriage.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Conceived' is there to compare the birth to the pregnancy: both were painless.

steps.title: Righteous women were not under חוה's curse
steps.stepSummary: From יוכבד's painless birth the גמרא learns that righteous women were not included in the punishment given to חוה, pain in childbirth.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here we learn that righteous women were not included in the sentence given to חוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a lesson from the answer it just gave. יוכבד's painless birth shows that righteous women are outside חוה's punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חוה was told that women would give birth in pain. Since יוכבד gave birth without pain, the גמרא learns that this punishment does not apply to righteous women.
steps.whatToRemember: Each phrase of שמות 2:1-2 teaches something. 'Took' means a full new wedding. 'Daughter' means יוכבד became young again at 130. 'Conceived' teaches that her birth was painless, which shows righteous women were not under חוה's curse.

phrases.english: From here we learn about righteous women
that they were not included in the sentence of Eve.
phrases.notes: בראשית 3:16, where חוה is told she will give birth in pain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general lesson from the painless birth taught in Step 26.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Righteous women are not included in חוה's punishment of painful childbirth, as shown by יוכבד.

steps.title: טוב was משה's real name
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק 'she saw that he was good' and brings a ברייתא. רבי מאיר says his name was טוב, and רבי יהודה says his name was טוביה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And she saw him that he was good.' A ברייתא teaches: רבי מאיר says, 'טוב' was his name. רבי יהודה says, 'טוביה' was his name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק about משה's birth and starts a list of opinions on what 'טוב' means. The first two opinions say it was simply his name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question behind the ברייתא is that every mother thinks her baby is good, so why does the פסוק bother to say it? רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה answer that the word is not praise at all. It is the name his parents gave him at birth: טוב, or the longer form טוביה.

keyTerms.meaning: Good. Here, possibly משה's birth name
Toviya, a longer form of the same name

phrases.english: "And she saw him, that he was good."
It was taught: Rabbi Meir says:
"Tov" was his name.
Rabbi Yehuda says: "Toviya" was his name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the topic of יוכבד's painless birth, the גמרא moves to the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, 'טוב' was משה's name. According to רבי יהודה, his name was טוביה.

steps.title: Fit for prophecy, or born circumcised
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה says 'good' means he was fit for prophecy. אחרים say it means he was born already circumcised.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה says: he was fit for prophecy. אחרים say: he was born already circumcised.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with two more opinions. These read 'טוב' as a special quality משה had, not as his name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה says his parents saw a spiritual greatness in him, meaning he was fit to become a נביא. אחרים point to a physical sign: he was born without a foreskin. Either way, 'good' describes something unusual about this baby.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others', a name used for certain unnamed תנאים

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya says: he was fit for prophecy.
Others say:
He was born already circumcised.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: More opinions in the same ברייתא. These give a quality instead of a name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'טוב' means משה was fit for prophecy (רבי נחמיה), or that he was born circumcised (אחרים).

steps.title: The house filled with light
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say that when משה was born, the whole house filled with light.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: at the time משה was born, the whole house was filled with light.
steps.whatsHappening: The last opinion in the ברייתא: 'good' refers to a miraculous light that filled the house at משה's birth. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the opinions in step 29, the חכמים read 'טוב' as something special. Here it is something seen in the room, not something about the baby's body or character. This fits the פסוק's word 'she saw'.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
At the time when Moshe was born,
the whole house was filled with light.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final opinion in the ברייתא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'טוב' refers to the light that filled the house when משה was born.

steps.title: The word 'טוב' links to the light of creation
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים prove their view by comparing two פסוקים. 'She saw him that he was טוב' matches 'God saw the light that it was טוב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written here: 'And she saw him that he was good.' And it is written there: 'And God saw the light, that it was good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the source for the חכמים. Both פסוקים use the same words, 'saw' and 'טוב'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the creation story, 'saw that it was good' is said about light. Because the same words appear at משה's birth, the חכמים read 'good' there as light too. This is a word-link between two פסוקים.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא gives five ways to read 'כי טוב הוא': his name was טוב, his name was טוביה, he was fit for prophecy, he was born circumcised, or the house filled with light.

phrases.aramaic: כְּתִיב הָכָא: ״וַתֵּרֶא אוֹתוֹ כִּי טוֹב הוּא״,
phrases.english: It is written here: "And she saw him, that he was good,"
and it is written there:
"And God saw the light, that it was good."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the חכמים' statement in step 30.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the house filled with light at משה's birth.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The same words, 'saw' and 'טוב', in בראשית 1:4, where they describe light.

steps.title: How she could hide him for three months
steps.stepSummary: יוכבד could hide משה for three months because the Egyptians started counting her pregnancy only from when עמרם took her back. She was already three months pregnant at that point.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And she hid him three months': because the Egyptians counted only from the time he took her back, and she had already been pregnant with him for three months from before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next words of the פסוק. It tells us how hiding the baby for three months was possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Egyptians watched pregnant women so they could find newborn boys. They thought יוכבד's pregnancy began at her remarriage and expected the birth nine months after that. Since she was already three months along, משה came three months 'early', and she had three months before they came looking.
steps.confusionAlert: The three months of hiding are after משה was born. They line up with the three months of pregnancy the Egyptians did not know about.

phrases.english: "And she hid him three months":
because the Egyptians did not count
except from the time that he took her back,
phrases.notes: 'He' is עמרם, who took יוכבד back as his wife.

phrases.english: but she was pregnant with him
for three months from before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the fact from step 25, that she was three months pregnant when עמרם took her back, to explain the next words of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her hidden three months of pregnancy gave her three months to hide the baby after he was born.

steps.title: Why couldn't she keep hiding him?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says she could not hide him any longer. The גמרא asks why not. She could have just kept on hiding him.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And she could no longer hide him.' Why? Let her hide him and keep going!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the next פסוק. If hiding worked for three months, what stopped her from going on?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 32 explained why the first three months were safe. But after the Egyptians began searching, a well-hidden baby should still be hidden. Something must have changed, and the next step explains what.

phrases.english: "And she could no longer hide him."
Why? Let her hide him and keep on going!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק and questions it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק's claim that she could no longer hide him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If hiding was possible for three months, nothing in the פסוק says why it suddenly became impossible.

steps.title: The Egyptians used crying babies
steps.stepSummary: Wherever the Egyptians heard a baby was born, they brought other babies there. The hidden baby would hear them, cry along, and be found.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, wherever the Egyptians heard that a baby had been born, they would bring babies there so that the hidden baby would hear them and cry together with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 33. The Egyptians had a trick that made hiding impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Babies tend to cry when they hear other babies crying. The Egyptians used this, so a hidden baby would give itself away. This is why יוכבד had no choice but to send משה away in a basket.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, כֹּל הֵיכָא דַּהֲווֹ שָׁמְעִי מִצְרָאֵי
phrases.english: Rather, anywhere that the Egyptians would hear
that a baby had been born,
they would bring babies there
so that it would hear them
and cry along with them,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כֹּל הֵיכָא דַּהֲווֹ שָׁמְעִי מִצְרָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a fact about the Egyptians' search method that explains the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A hidden baby could stay hidden forever.
steps.terutzMaskana: Crying babies were brought to make the hidden baby cry, so hiding became impossible.

steps.title: The little foxes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports this with the פסוק 'Catch us the foxes, the little foxes', which it reads as a hint to the babies the Egyptians used.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Catch us the foxes, the little foxes...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a פסוק as a hint to the Egyptian trick from step 34.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'little foxes' are read as the small babies the Egyptians used to hunt down the Jewish babies. The פסוק describes small creatures that cause damage, which fits the babies brought to expose the hidden ones.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc., the rest of the פסוק

phrases.english: as it is written: "Catch us the foxes,
the little foxes, etc."
phrases.notes: The 'little foxes' stand for the small babies the Egyptians brought to catch the hidden ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a פסוק as support for the answer in step 34.
steps.raayaObject: The Egyptians used small babies to find the hidden ones.

steps.title: Why a basket of reeds?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says she took a basket made of גומא (reeds). The גמרא asks what was special about that material.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And she took for him a basket of reeds.' What is different about reeds?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the פסוק and asks why she chose reeds. This sets up רבי אלעזר's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names the material for no obvious reason. Reeds are cheap and fragile, so the גמרא wants to know what the choice teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Reeds, papyrus, a cheap plant material

phrases.english: "And she took for him a basket of reeds."
What is different about reeds?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the basket was made of cheap reeds.

steps.title: צדיקים value their money
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says this teaches that צדיקים care about their money even more than about their bodies. She used a cheap material instead of spending more.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: from here we learn about צדיקים that their money is more precious to them than their bodies.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question of step 36 and draws a lesson about צדיקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She was saving her own child, yet she still chose the cheapest material. רבי אלעזר learns that צדיקים are very careful not to waste their money. The next steps explain why.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
From here we learn about righteous people
that their money is more precious to them than their bodies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 36.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She chose cheap reeds because צדיקים are careful with their money.

steps.title: Why do they care so much?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why צדיקים care so much about their money.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why all this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short follow-up question. It sets up the reason that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Valuing money more than your body sounds strange, or even greedy. The question asks for the reason, so we do not misunderstand רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: And why so much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רבי אלעזר's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why צדיקים treat their money as so precious.

steps.title: Because they never take what isn't theirs
steps.stepSummary: צדיקים value their money because they never steal, so every coin they have was earned honestly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they do not stretch out their hands to stolen property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for step 37 and ends the section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since צדיקים never take anything that is not theirs, all their money comes from honest work and is hard to replace. That is why they are careful not to waste it. It is not greed but honesty.
steps.whatToRemember: The cheap reed basket teaches that צדיקים are careful with their money, because they never take what belongs to others.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean צדיקים love money. Their honest money is precious because they refuse to get any money in a dishonest way.

phrases.english: Because they do not stretch out their hands to stolen property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 38.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They never take stolen property, so all their money is honestly earned and precious to them.

steps.title: A second reason for using reeds: soft material survives bumps
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני explains that she chose גומא because a soft material can withstand hitting both soft and hard things.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: She chose a soft material, because it can hold up when it bumps into something soft and also when it bumps into something hard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the question from step 36: why did she make the basket from גומא?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said she used גומא to save money. רבי שמואל בר נחמני gives a practical reason instead. A hard material like wood could crack if it hit a rock, but a soft material bends and survives.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:
A soft material was chosen,
which is able to withstand

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְנֵי דָּבָר רַךְ וּבִפְנֵי דָּבָר קָשֶׁה.
phrases.english: bumping into a soft thing and bumping into a hard thing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר: דָּבָר רַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the question of step 36, alongside רבי אלעזר's answer in step 37.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the basket was made of גומא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Soft material can survive hitting both soft and hard objects in the water.

steps.title: Why the bad-smelling pitch went on the outside
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that חמר was put inside and זפת outside so that משה would not smell a bad odor.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'She coated it with bitumen and with pitch.' A Sage taught: the bitumen was on the inside and the pitch was on the outside, so that the צדיק would not smell a bad smell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the פסוק and quotes a ברייתא explaining why two coatings were used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions two materials, which raises the question of why both were needed. The ברייתא answers that each had its own place. The smelly זפת was kept outside so baby משה would not have to smell it.

keyTerms.meaning: Bitumen, a sticky coating without a bad smell
Pitch, a sealing tar with a strong bad smell

phrases.english: "And she coated it with bitumen and with pitch,"
A Sage taught:
bitumen on the inside
and pitch on the outside,
so that he would not smell
that righteous one, a bad smell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the same פסוק, moving on to the coatings of the basket.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bitumen went inside and pitch outside, so that משה would not smell a bad odor.

steps.title: What does 'בסוף' mean? רבי אלעזר says ים סוף
steps.stepSummary: On the words 'she placed it בסוף', רבי אלעזר says this means ים סוף. רבי שמואל בר נחמני then starts to give a different opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'She put the child in it and placed it in the סוף.' רבי אלעזר says: this means ים סוף. רבי שמואל בר נחמני said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the פסוק and brings רבי אלעזר's reading of the word 'סוף'. It is also setting up a disagreement, because רבי שמואל בר נחמני begins a second opinion that continues right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning of 'סוף' is reeds by the riverbank. רבי אלעזר reads it as the name of a sea, ים סוף. The amud ends just as רבי שמואל בר נחמני starts to answer, and his view continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Reeds; also part of the name ים סוף
The Sea of Reeds (the Red Sea)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop at רבי אלעזר. This is the start of a disagreement, and רבי שמואל בר נחמני's view comes right after these words.

phrases.english: "And she put the child in it
and placed it in the reeds,"
Rabbi Elazar says: the Sea of Suf.
phrases.notes: He reads the word סוף as the name of ים סוף, not just reeds.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:

steps.triggerLanguage: וַתָּשֶׂם בָּהּ אֶת הַיֶּלֶד וַתָּשֶׂם בַּסּוּף רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the same פסוק and opens a new disagreement about the word 'סוף'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר: 'בסוף' means she placed him in ים סוף.
